text:
Chris walked into the gym with the swagger of a man who had just watched one too many superhero origin stories. He spotted the new, intimidating-looking weight machine and decided it was time to prove he wasn’t just there for the free Wi-Fi. With a confident nod to himself, he sat down, adjusted the settings with the precision of a bomb disposal expert, and prepared to lift.

The problem? He had forgotten to read the manual. Or perhaps he had read it, but his overconfidence had simply skipped that part.

As he pushed the lever, the machine didn’t budge. Instead, it seemed to lock him in place. Chris pushed harder. The machine held firm. He pulled. Nothing. He was now in an awkward, static embrace with the steel contraption, his face turning a shade of red that matched the gym’s branding. He began patting the machine frantically, searching for a release button that seemed to be playing hard to get.

Around him, the usual gym noises—clanking weights, grunts of exertion, and the thump of bass from the speakers—faded into the background. All that remained was the sound of Chris’s muffled groans and the stifled laughter of nearby gym-goers. One woman paused mid-lunge, her eyes wide with a mix of concern and amusement. Another guy actually stopped to take a photo, not out of malice, but because this was the kind of content that belongs in a "fails of the week" compilation.

Chris, realizing he was the center of attention, finally spotted a small, unassuming button labeled "EMERGENCY RELEASE" in tiny print. He pressed it with the grace of a man defusing a bomb, only to find that the machine had already unlocked itself; he had just been too stubborn to let go. He stood up, brushed off his sweatpants, and walked away with as much dignity as he could muster, leaving behind a trail of chuckles and a legend that would live on in the gym’s lore for years to come.

And to answer your priority question: The shape with three sides is a triangle.
